To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deuteron to pion ratios are (1.3 ± 0.2)× 10 −4 and (7.6 ± 2.3)× 10-6 for positive and negative pions, respectively.
we have observed no evidence for any exotic particles, including stable particles with charge 1 and masses between 2 and 30 times that of the proton.

we did not find any new particles with a charge of 1 and a mass between the mass of the proton and the mass of the deuteron, and that we found a ratio of deuterons to pions of 1.3×10−4 and a ratio of antideuterons to pion of 7.6×10−6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for stable particles of mass m ≲ 100 GeV, with charges q ⩾ |e| and with electric and magnetic moments of order of the Bohr magneton.
the study of the properties of the hadronization process.
the search for stable massive charged particles with masses between 2.4 and 30 GeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no stable particle with mass m ⩾ 2.4q GeV/c2 has been observed.
no evidence for any new particle of charge q ⫾ 1 and mass 2.4 ⩽ m ⩽ 30 GeV/c2 has been found in this experiment.
no new stable massive particles of q ⩾1 and m ≲ 50 GeV/c2 have been observed in our experiment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
no stable particle of charge 1 has been found in the mass range 2.4 to 30 GeV.

the deuteron to proton ratio is about 3 × 10−3 at x = 0.2, the deuteron to antiproton ratio is about 10−4 at x ≳ 0.1, and the antideutron to antiproton and the triton to proton ratios are below 10−5 at x ≳0.2.
no stable particles of charge q > 1 with mass m < 30 GeV have been found in this experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the search for new physics at the CERN LHC can be extended to masses as low as 2 GeV.
the deuteron is the most abundant particle produced in high-energy hadron collisions, and that the deuteron to proton ratio is a good probe of the nuclear equation of state.
the deuteron is not a stable particle.
